claim.statement: Per the United Nations as of early April 2026, more than 120,000 Afghan migrants had been deported from Iran in the first three months of 2026 — a pace of roughly 1,300 deportations per day.
claim.subject: Iran-deported Afghan migrants Q1 2026

evidence.summary: Frontier Post citing UN figure for first three months of 2026.

claim.statement: Persian-language outlets reported on 18-19 April 2026 that approximately 6,000–7,000 Afghan migrants were deported from Iran (and Pakistan) in a single day, indicating sustained mass-expulsion tempo throughout the post-ceasefire window.
claim.subject: Afghan migrants deported in one day

evidence.summary: Salam Watandar: >7,000 reported the next day.

claim.statement: On 29 April 2026, Persian financial outlet Jahan-Sanat reported a nationwide shutdown across Tehran Bazaar protesting the rial collapse — a historically loaded signal, given that bazaar shutdowns famously preceded the 1979 revolution.
claim.subject: Tehran Bazaar merchants

evidence.summary: Jahan-Sanat: nationwide closure of Tehran Bazaar; FX-rate protest intensifies.
Two days earlier (Apr 27): ISNA, Fars, IRNA all reported merchant gatherings in Tehran Bazaar.

claim.statement: On 30 April 2026 the Universal House of Justice publicly stated that two young Bahá'í cousins held in Iran — Peyvand Naimi (a swimmer, arrested 18 Dey 1404 and transferred to IRGC intelligence detention) and Borna Naimi (a karate champion, arrested 10 Esfand 1404 at his workplace) — face execution.
claim.subject: Peyvand and Borna Naimi

evidence.summary: Iran International (Persian) carries the Universal House of Justice statement in full.

assessment.uncertainty: Bahá'í governing-body statement; sentencing details and current trial-stage may shift.

claim.statement: In April 2026, three Bahá'í women in Kerman entered prison to serve sentences, part of a sustained pattern of Bahá'í-targeted detentions across multiple Iranian provinces (Kerman, Mashhad, Shiraz, Isfahan).
claim.subject: 3 Bahá'í women in Kerman

claim.statement: On 28 April 2026 the Iranian government announced new fines for soldiers absent or runaway from mandatory service (sarbazi), suggesting that desertion or absenteeism has reached a level requiring fresh enforcement levers in the post-war atmosphere.
claim.subject: Government of Iran

evidence.summary: Moniban (via Vista) reports the new fine schedule.

assessment.uncertainty: Direction of change (raised vs. created) unclear from headline alone; the policy itself is the diagnostic.

claim.statement: On 22 April 2026 the deputy commander of the IRGC publicly warned women that hijab is 'God's own command', signalling that the post-war regime intends to re-tighten compulsory veiling rather than relax it under economic pressure.
claim.subject: IRGC deputy commander
claim.object: women — hijab is God's own command

evidence.summary: Sharq Daily summary of the IRGC deputy commander's remarks.

claim.statement: Iran International described the post-war regime's gender-policy posture as a deliberate 'occupation of urban spaces' and 'return to the 60s under the shadow of war propaganda' — a framing that pairs the IRGC hijab warning with documented street-level enforcement in Tehran.
claim.subject: Iranian regime gender posture

assessment.uncertainty: Diaspora-outlet framing; pair with on-the-ground reports of fines/vehicle impoundment for a stronger triangulation.

claim.statement: On 27 April 2026, IRIB-affiliated outlet Jam-e Jam published that there had been a 'third American-Zionist enemy attack' against IRIB — a regime-side acknowledgment that state broadcasting has been hit at least three times during the war and post-ceasefire period.
claim.subject: IRIB

assessment.uncertainty: Regime-side count; technical detail of 'attack' unspecified.

claim.statement: On or shortly before 29 April 2026, hackers — widely attributed to the Israel-aligned Predatory Sparrow ('گنجشک درنده') group — disrupted Iran state TV (IRIB) to broadcast a speech by exiled crown prince Reza Pahlavi, an unprecedented penetration of regime broadcasting in the post-ceasefire phase.
claim.subject: Hackers (likely Predatory Sparrow)
claim.object: IRIB broadcast to air Reza Pahlavi speech

evidence.summary: FRANCE 24 mirror: 'Hackers disrupt Iran state TV to broadcast exiled crown prince'.
IRIB-side acknowledgment of repeated attacks corroborates that disruptions occurred.

assessment.uncertainty: Attribution to Predatory Sparrow not confirmed in source; broadcast-content authenticity reported but unverified.

claim.statement: On 24 April 2026 the U.S. Treasury added approximately 20 companies and 19 ships of Iran's so-called 'shadow fleet' to its sanctions list, including the independent Chinese refinery Hengli Petrochemical (Dalian) for sustained large-scale Iranian-oil purchases.
claim.subject: U.S. Treasury

claim.statement: On 25 April 2026, U.S. Central Command publicly stated that the M/V Sevan — one of the 19 shadow-fleet vessels sanctioned the previous day — had been intercepted by a U.S. Navy helicopter from the guided-missile destroyer Pinckney in the Arabian Sea and forced to turn back.
claim.subject: U.S. CENTCOM

evidence.summary: Persian-language X reposting of CENTCOM statement.

claim.statement: By 22 April 2026, Bloomberg reported that Iranian oil tankers had begun systematically going dark (turning off AIS transponders) to slip past the US blockade laden with crude — and by 28 April, Bloomberg observed tankers clustering just shy of the blockade line off Chabahar port awaiting an opportunity to break through.
claim.subject: Iranian shadow-fleet tankers

claim.statement: On 21 April 2026 a senior Iranian reformist leader publicly called for 'courage in flexibility' rather than 'endless confrontation' — language explicitly framing negotiated retreat as a national-survival imperative, and adding to the Rouhani 'great change' line as a second establishment-pragmatist break with the IRGC posture.
claim.subject: Iranian reformist leader

assessment.uncertainty: Specific named leader not identified in headline; verify with subsequent Persian-language coverage.

claim.statement: Regime-affiliated outlet SNN published an unusually emphatic 1 May 2026 message from the Shahr-e Rey prayer field telling 'Imam Khamenei: whenever you wish, we are in the field and will not empty the streets' — conspicuous over-emphasis on attendance suggests Friday-prayer attendance has actually been thinning.
claim.subject: Regime mouthpiece (SNN)

evidence.summary: SNN headline emphasising 'we will not empty the streets' — diagnostic of strain.

assessment.uncertainty: Inference from regime over-emphasis; needs corroborating attendance counts or photos.

operations.rationale: Tehran Bazaar shutdown is downstream of currency collapse, which is downstream of oil-export squeeze (tankers going dark to evade blockade caps revenue).
IRGC deputy's official threat instantiates the analytical claim that the regime is reverting to 1980s-style enforcement.
Predatory-Sparrow IRIB hijack is one of the attacks the regime acknowledged on 27 April.
Sevan interception followed directly from prior-day Treasury sanctions designating that vessel.

question.text: Does the 29 Apr Tehran Bazaar shutdown spread (Tabriz, Mashhad, Isfahan bazaars) and persist for >5 days, the way 1978 bazaar strikes did?
question.resolution_criteria: Daily open/closed reports from major provincial bazaars; ISNA/Fars/IRNA wires; merchant-association statements.
question.why_it_matters: Persisting, multi-city bazaar strike was the proximate detonator of the 1979 revolution; it is the single highest-signal commercial-class indicator.

question.text: Will the Naimi cousins be executed, sentenced to long imprisonment, or released as part of post-war optics?
question.resolution_criteria: Court sentencing announcement; Bahá'í International Community press releases; IRGC intelligence release/transfer reports.

question.text: Is the new conscript-fine policy a response to mass desertion, or a routine fee adjustment? What is the actual desertion rate post-war?
question.resolution_criteria: Persian-language military forums; sarbazi exemption volume; defence-ministry spokesperson statements; family-network Telegram channels.

question.text: Can the shadow fleet sustain Iran's ~$30B/year oil-export volume against a hardening US blockade + Treasury sanctions, or does export volume collapse below the regime's fiscal break-even?
question.resolution_criteria: Lloyd's List shadow-fleet AIS data; Bloomberg / Al Jazeera tracker investigations; Treasury OFAC weekly designations.

question.text: Will the IRGC's 'God's command' hijab line trigger a fresh phase of Zhina-style street defiance, or is post-war fatigue / bandwidth elsewhere keeping women's resistance latent?
question.resolution_criteria: Hijab-defiance video volume on diaspora channels; gasht-ershad fine totals; named-arrest trickle from women's-movement Telegram networks.

synthesis.title: Cracks at the margins, 17 Apr – 1 May 2026 — bazaar, Bahá'ís, conscripts, oil, IRIB, Afghans
synthesis.summary: Pulling on the under-covered seams: (a) Tehran Bazaar — historically the single most loaded commercial-class signal in Iranian regime collapse — shut down nationwide on 29 Apr in protest of the rial collapse, after merchant gatherings on 20 and 27 Apr (ISNA/Fars/IRNA on the regime side, Jahan-Sanat on the dissent side). (b) Bahá'í minority pressure intensified: the Universal House of Justice publicly named two Bahá'í cousins, Peyvand and Borna Naimi, as facing execution; three Bahá'í women jailed in Kerman; sustained detentions in Mashhad, Shiraz, Isfahan. (c) Conscription strain visible in policy: on 28 Apr the regime announced fresh fines for absent or runaway conscripts — a tightening rarely reached for unless desertion is real. (d) Oil dark-fleet under sustained pressure: 24 Apr Treasury sanctions on ~20 companies and 19 ships including Hengli (Dalian); 25 Apr CENTCOM interception of M/V Sevan; tankers systematically going dark per Bloomberg, clustering shy of the blockade line off Chabahar. (e) IRIB compromise public: an IRIB-affiliated outlet acknowledged a 'third American-Zionist attack' on state TV on 27 Apr; France 24 (mirrored) reports state TV was hijacked to broadcast a Reza Pahlavi speech ~29 Apr — likely Predatory Sparrow. (f) Afghan migrants as the regime's pressure-release valve: per the UN, >120,000 deported in Q1 2026, with single-day expulsions of 6,000–7,000 reported on 18-19 Apr — classic crisis scapegoating. (g) Hijab posture re-tightened: IRGC deputy commander warned women on 22 Apr that hijab is 'God's own command'; Iran International framed the post-war regime as 'returning to the 60s' on gender. (h) A second elite-defection signal: a senior reformist publicly called for 'courage in flexibility, not endless confrontation' on 21 Apr — paralleling Rouhani's 'great change'. (i) Friday-prayer optics: regime mouthpiece SNN aired an unusually loud 1 May line about 'not emptying the streets' — its emphasis itself diagnostic. Together these sit underneath the headline cracks (command vacuum, currency collapse, labour, infrastructure, clergy defection, students, prisons, pharma, cyber, Kurdistan) — i.e., the regime's external valves (oil, refugees, broadcasting) and its internal coercion levers (Bahá'í minority, hijab, conscripts) are simultaneously stressed, while the bazaar is starting to blink red.
synthesis.limitations: Two-week window. Persian on-the-ground signal is dampened by the national internet blackout; reliance on diaspora outlets (Iran International, Hengaw, Kayhan London) and regime-side counter-mouthpieces (Jam-e Jam, SNN, Sharq Daily) is mitigated by recording each side's framing alongside the other. Bazaar closure scope (Tehran-only vs. multi-city) and IRIB-hijack provenance (Predatory Sparrow attribution) carry the largest residual uncertainty.
